text: Henry Nolan’s motive to evoke nostalgia and a sense of belonging is structurally reinforced by his use of the old mill as a central metaphor. By positioning the mill as a symbol of stability and resistance against modernity, Nolan creates a thematic framework where tradition and community are not just abstract concepts but tangible anchors in a rapidly changing world. This structural choice directly serves his intent to highlight the importance of preserving heritage, thereby linking his desire for emotional resonance with a narrative architecture that contrasts the enduring past with the disruptive present.
